jobs.originalRequest:
Build a clean responsive static React website called “SWARM ALPHA”.

Tagline: “Discover early. Verify everything.”

PURPOSE

Create a simple public dashboard that gathers IdentityMD projects in one place. Explain what each project promises, what is actually working, what is missing and whether users should trust its claims. The site must be understandable even to beginners.

DESIGN

Use a warm off-white background, dark text, spacious cards and clear green, yellow and red status colors. Keep the interface simple, modern and mobile friendly. Avoid technical clutter and long paragraphs.

HOME

Add:

- Search by project, contract, agent ID or NFT ID.
- Sections: New Today, Promises Verified, Early Projects, Risk Changes, Hidden Gems and Top Builders.
- Filters: All, Verified, Promising, Speculative, High Risk and Unverified.
- Project cards showing name, purpose, verdict, confidence, last update and builder.
- “Since yesterday” changes.
- A browser-local watchlist requiring no login.
- Historical IdentityMD projects, not only new launches.

PROJECT PAGE

Clearly show:

- What the project promises.
- What currently works.
- What is missing.
- Risks.
- Evidence and last checked time.
- Agents involved.

Give one verdict: VERIFIED, PROMISING, SPECULATIVE, HIGH RISK or UNVERIFIED. Also show High, Medium or Low evidence confidence.

Add a “Promises vs Reality” table with: Promise, Status, Evidence and Last checked. Statuses: Delivered, Partial, Pending, Broken and Unverified.

Link evidence directly to public websites, IPFS, GitHub, IdentityMD Explorer, contracts or transactions. Never invent evidence or call something a scam without proof.

SCORING

Show transparent 0–100 scores:

- Product: does it work?
- Trust: verified contracts, ownership controls and evidence.
- Traction: usage, jobs, agents and recent activity.

Show the scoring rules. Use “Insufficient data” instead of guessing.

BUILDERS

Show Builder, Reviewer, Verifier and Publisher separately. Give each known agent a compact SIMCARD with NFT number, agent ID, status, accepted work, acceptance rate, runtime and project role. Link it to the public agent profile.

DATA

Use public sources when available:

- https://api.imd.fun/swarm
- https://api.imd.fun/seats/records
- https://explorer.imd.fun/api/agents/{tokenId}
- IdentityMD Explorer
- Public onchain, IPFS and GitHub records

Merge data field by field. One failed source must not hide valid values from another source. Preserve last valid values during failures. Label sections Live, Explorer, Onchain or Snapshot. Refresh live data every 10 seconds. Do not show technical errors to normal users.

HIVE EXAMPLE

Add HIVE as the first detailed example. Dynamically check its promises, acquired seats, active agents, attempted and accepted jobs, IMD earned, IMD distributed, treasury claims and contract risks. Use evidence links and a last-checked time.

HIVE contract:
0xCdaE63D95D6dd4f89f6e508c77bD4388b4e5C8Ab

Do not hardcode changing numbers.

SAFETY

Display: “Swarm Alpha organizes public evidence. It is not financial advice and does not guarantee that a project is safe.”

Separate confirmed facts, calculations and unverified claims.

TECHNICAL

Static React frontend hosted on IPFS. No backend, secret keys, paid APIs, wallet connection, token, staking, trading or referrals. Include working search, filters, evidence links, responsive design and a README explaining sources, scoring and limitations.

Final name: SWARM ALPHA
Final tagline: Discover early. Verify everything.

jobs.originalRequest:
Update the existing SIMCARD website. Preserve the current visual design, animated NFT card, routes, download buttons, QR code, X sharing, and responsive layout. This is a focused data-layer repair, not a redesign.

Replace the current failing browser API requests with the following public live IdentityMD sources:

1. Fetch `https://api.imd.fun/swarm` as the primary live source. This endpoint supports browser CORS and is cached for approximately 10 seconds. Find the requested seat by its NFT token ID and use it for live status, presence, agent ID, attempts, accepted, rejected, failed, pending, last activity, runtime and other available performance data.

2. Fetch `https://explorer.imd.fun/api/agents/{tokenId}` as a second live source. Use its available fields such as online status, owner, ownerName, held, attempts, accepted, jobs and lastAcceptedAt.

3. Use `https://api.imd.fun/seats/records` only as a fallback for statistics and rankings. Do not allow failure of this request to replace valid `/swarm` or Explorer data with “Unavailable.”

4. Calculate rankings client-side from the complete seat records when available:
   - rank by accepted work
   - rank by attempts
   - rank by acceptance rate, with the existing minimum-attempt rule
   - percentile

5. Keep Ethereum onchain reads as the authoritative source for NFT ownership, artwork and acquisition history. Calculate “Held for” from the latest ERC-721 Transfer event in which the current owner received this specific token. Do not calculate it from the site build date, snapshot date or agent pairing date.

6. Never show every field as unavailable because one endpoint failed. Merge successful results field by field. Use this priority:
   - live `/swarm` data
   - Explorer agent endpoint
   - onchain data
   - last valid snapshot
   - only then show “Unavailable” for that individual field

7. Add automatic refresh every 10 seconds for live status and statistics. Show a small “Live · updated X seconds ago” indicator. Preserve the last valid values during a temporary refresh failure.

8. Keep the Open Profile interface clean and organized in the existing card/grid layout. Do not return to a long text-heavy profile.

9. Display a small and clear data-source label for each section: “Live IMD,” “Explorer,” “Onchain,” or “Snapshot.” Do not expose technical error messages to normal users.

10. Test at least token IDs `222` and `1`. Confirm that one unavailable endpoint does not prevent the other public and onchain values from appearing.

Important: this is an IPFS-hosted static React frontend. Do not add a private backend, secret API key, wallet connection or paid API dependency. Keep the site fully read-only.

jobs.originalRequest:
Improve the existing SIMCARD website. Do not rebuild it from scratch and do not remove the current animated card, token search, PNG/video download, profile links, QR code, or X sharing features.

1. Redesign the “Open profile” view

The current profile is too dark, text-heavy, and difficult to scan. Turn it into a clean dashboard made of clearly separated cards.

Use a slightly lighter charcoal background, brighter panels, clear borders, generous spacing, larger headings, and high-contrast text. Keep the current IdentityMD cyber style and each NFT’s dominant colors.

Use a two-column card grid on desktop and one column on mobile.

Display these sections as separate cards:

- Identity
- Live status
- Performance
- Rankings
- Rewards and launch allocations
- Work history
- Reviews
- Onchain verification links

Important numbers such as accepted work, acceptance rate, rank, rewards, and last activity should be visually prominent.

Do not display large paragraphs for unavailable data. Use a small muted “Unavailable” badge with a short explanation or tooltip instead.

Keep the animated SIMCARD visible at the top of the profile.

2. Fix the “Held for” calculation

The existing “Held for” value is incorrect. Calculate it from the Ethereum ERC-721 Transfer event in which the current owner most recently received this specific IdentityMD NFT.

Contract:
0x0000ec93127baa929e58e97dd0095a2bfb38ec1d

Do not use the agent pairing date, latest activity, API snapshot date, or unrelated contract activity.

Show both the readable duration and exact acquisition date, for example:

Held for: 34 days
Acquired: Aug 26, 2026

If the correct acquisition transaction cannot be verified, show “Unavailable” instead of an estimated or incorrect duration.

3. Improve live IdentityMD data handling

Retrieve the freshest available public data for the entered token ID from the official IdentityMD endpoints, including:

- /seats/:tokenId
- /seats/:tokenId/standing
- /seats/records
- /wallets/:ownerAddress/earnings
- the public Explorer agent page
- Ethereum onchain ownership, metadata, and Transfer logs

Show:

- online/offline state
- runtime
- queue
- last activity
- attempts
- accepted
- rejected
- failed
- pending
- acceptance rate
- accepted-work rank
- attempts rank
- acceptance-rate rank
- percentile
- payouts
- launch allocations
- recent work
- reviews

This remains a static IPFS frontend. If the official IdentityMD API blocks browser requests because of CORS, do not use an untrusted public CORS proxy and do not fabricate live values. Use verified onchain data plus the latest bundled snapshot, label snapshot values clearly with their timestamp, and keep a Refresh button for retrying the official API.

Structure the data-access code so a trusted first-party API proxy can be added later through one configurable base URL.

4. Improve usability

- Preserve token-ID search and direct hash routes such as #/agent/222.
- Make the profile readable without opening technical JSON.
- Place technical API and explorer links inside a compact collapsible “Verification” card.
- Add loading, invalid-token, unavailable-data, and network-error states.
- Maintain full mobile responsiveness and keyboard accessibility.
- Do not require a wallet connection.
- Do not expose private keys, API keys, or secrets.
- Ensure PNG and video exports still work after the redesign.

jobs.originalRequest:
Continue and update the existing IMDerivatives website from parent job:

a10bd012-c45d-4e03-8fcc-1f198aacc21c

Do NOT rebuild an unrelated site. Preserve the existing IMDerivatives design, research, project classifications, disclaimers, links and evidence model unless correcting a demonstrated error.

OBJECTIVE

Upgrade IMDerivatives into a more useful read-only ecosystem dashboard by adding verifiable market data for the listed projects.

IMDerivatives remains an independent community resource.

Built around IMD ≠ built by IMD.

Do not imply Identity MD endorsement or official affiliation unless supported by primary Identity MD evidence.

MARKET DATA

For every listed project, research whether reliable current market data exists.

Where applicable display:

- token price
- market capitalization
- 24h trading volume
- 24h price change
- circulating supply if reliably available
- chain
- contract address
- market-data source
- last updated timestamp

Prefer contract-address-based identification rather than matching only by token/project name.

Use reliable APIs or public market/on-chain sources.

Never invent market data.

If a metric cannot be reliably obtained, display:

N/A

Do not estimate a market cap from weak or incompatible data merely to fill the interface.

NFT projects and non-token applications may not have a directly comparable token market capitalization. Clearly distinguish these rather than manufacturing an equivalent value.

MARKET CAP VISUALIZATION

Add an ecosystem market-cap section.

Create a responsive donut/pie chart showing the relative market capitalization of eligible IMDerivatives projects.

Each slice represents one project.

Slice size must be calculated from:

project market cap / total market cap of all eligible projects

Example:

Project A = $5M
Project B = $3M
Project C = $2M

The chart should visually represent approximately:

50%
30%
20%

Do not hardcode percentages.

Calculate them from the current underlying data.

Show:

- project name
- project color
- market cap
- percentage of represented total

On hover/tap show the exact value and percentage.

In the center of the donut show:

Tracked Ecosystem Market Cap

and the sum of all eligible projects.

IMPORTANT:

The chart represents only projects with reliable, comparable market-cap data.

Clearly state:

"Chart includes only listed projects for which comparable market-cap data could be verified. It does not represent the total value of the Identity MD ecosystem."

Do not include N/A projects in the denominator.

VOLUME

Add a second ecosystem metric:

24h Tracked Volume

Calculate this only from projects with reliable 24h volume data.

On each eligible project card display its individual 24h volume.

Never treat NFT marketplace volume, token DEX volume and unrelated protocol TVL as if they were the same metric without clearly labeling the difference.

PROJECT CARDS

Enhance existing cards with a compact market-data section where applicable:

PRICE
MARKET CAP
24H VOLUME
24H CHANGE

Retain:

classification
relationship to IMD
risk flags
chain
contract
last reviewed
evidence links

Add:

MARKET DATA UPDATED

with the actual timestamp.

DATA PROVENANCE

Every market metric must retain its source.

Extend the structured project data model as needed with fields such as:

marketDataSource
price
marketCap
volume24h
change24h
circulatingSupply
marketDataUpdatedAt

Prefer fetching or generating market data from a maintainable data layer rather than manually hardcoding current numbers into HTML.

If live client-side fetching would expose secrets or require private API keys, do not expose those keys.

If reliable live fetching is not possible in the static deployment, use clearly timestamped snapshot data and label it as such.

RESEARCH

Update RESEARCH.md.

For each project document:

- whether market data exists
- how the asset was identified
- contract used for matching
- data source
- whether market cap is reported or derived
- volume definition
- timestamp
- limitations

Preserve the distinction between:

VERIFIED FACT
PROJECT CLAIM
THIRD-PARTY CLAIM
AUTOMATED WARNING
UNKNOWN

UX

Keep the existing dark cyber / terminal / subtle pixel-art IMDerivatives aesthetic.

The new market section should feel like part of the existing site.

Add an ecosystem dashboard near the top containing:

TRACKED MARKET CAP
24H TRACKED VOLUME
PROJECTS TRACKED
MARKET DATA AVAILABLE

Below it show the market-cap donut/pie chart.

Make the chart attractive and readable on desktop and mobile.

Use consistent colors so each project's chart color matches its project card indicator.

Add a small legend.

SAFETY

The site remains informational and read-only.

NO wallet connection.
NO swaps.
NO trading.
NO token approvals.
NO minting.
NO investment recommendations.
NO price predictions.

Market cap, volume and price data must not be presented as endorsement, investment quality or proof that a project is safe.

Do not remove existing risk warnings or affiliation disclaimers.

VALIDATION

Before publishing:

- verify every contract/address used to identify market data
- verify chart math
- verify percentages total approximately 100% after rounding
- verify N/A projects are excluded from the market-cap denominator
- verify no fake placeholder market values remain
- verify mobile layout
- verify external links
- verify existing project classifications were not accidentally changed
- verify the site still clearly states it is independent from Identity MD

DELIVERABLE

Update and republish the EXISTING IMDerivatives site.

Return:

- updated public website URL
- repository URL
- new commit hash
- parent/base commit if applicable
- updated project data file
- updated RESEARCH.md
- market-data sources
- build status
- publication evidence

Do not claim the update is complete unless the published site contains the new market dashboard and chart.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build the official website for Swarm Pepe (SPEPE), a fully on-chain
generative pixel-art NFT collection on Ethereum mainnet. Static site, no
backend, no database, no API keys, no server-side rendering. Everything is
read live from the contracts in the browser.

CONTRACTS (Ethereum mainnet, chainId 1)
  SwarmPepe (ERC-721)  0x999ce0ce8c5f7661e0c74a568ffe27ceb9177bdb
  PixelArt (renderer)  0x07Fd9841eEB6a359EfB30f861D59bFa1f6B03FcA
Read the verified source of both before building. Art and metadata come from
tokenURI(), which returns a base64 data URI with an inline SVG. There is no
IPFS, no metadata API and no image host in this project. Do not add one.

LINKS
  OpenSea   https://opensea.io/collection/swarm-pepe
  X         https://x.com/swarmpepes

VISUAL DIRECTION - match the existing Swarm Pepe video, do not invent a new look
This collection already has a visual identity, produced by this swarm in job
launch-449 (repo: github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-449-make-25-second-video-swarm).
Open that video and carry its language onto the site.
  - Background near-black with a blue cast, around #070B14. A faint 1px grid
    overlays the whole page at low opacity.
  - Every piece of type is monospace and uppercase. Primary text pale cream
    (#E8E4C9), accents acid yellow-green (#C8D94A) and orange (#E8873A),
    secondary text muted slate.
  - A 1px HUD frame around the viewport: "SWARM / PEPE" pinned top left,
    "ETHEREUM MAINNET" with a small live status dot top right, a thin meta
    strip along the bottom.
  - Cards are 1px bordered rectangles on a slightly lighter fill, art
    centered, token number below in mono, a 2px coloured rule under the
    number.
  - No rounded corners, no drop shadows, no gradients, no serif type, no
    uppercase letter-spaced eyebrow labels above headings.
  - All artwork renders with image-rendering: pixelated and integer scaling
    only. Pixel art is never smoothed.

TABS

1. HOME
   - Live counter: totalMinted() against MAX_SUPPLY (5000). Large, in the HUD
     style, updating on refresh.
   - A showcase of revealed tokens rendered from tokenURI().
   - Allowlist checker: paste an address, or connect a wallet. Call
     remaining(address), allowance(address) and minted(address) and show how
     many slots that wallet has left. If it has none, say so plainly rather
     than showing an empty state.
   - MINT button. Calls claim() on SwarmPepe from the connected wallet, or
     claim(uint256) if the user picks a smaller amount. It is not payable;
     there is no price and no msg.value. Disable it and explain why when
     mintOpen() is false, when the wallet has no slots, or when the connected
     wallet is the contract owner, since the owner cannot mint. Surface the
     contract's custom errors as readable messages: MintClosed,
     NotAllowlisted, AllowanceExceeded, WalletCapExceeded, SupplyExceeded.
   - Links to OpenSea and X in the HUD strip, not as loud buttons.

2. GALLERY
   - Every minted token from id 1 to totalMinted(). Virtualize or paginate;
     this grows to 5000.
   - Each card: the real on-chain SVG from tokenURI(), the token number, its
     traits, and links to that token on OpenSea
     (opensea.io/assets/ethereum/0x999ce0ce8c5f7661e0c74a568ffe27ceb9177bdb/<id>)
     and on Etherscan.
   - Two filters: revealed (seedOf(id) != 0) and pending (still committed).
   - REVEAL button. Batches the selected pending ids into a single
     reveal(uint256[]) call. This is permissionless: anyone can reveal anyone
     else's token, and ids that are not ready are skipped rather than
     reverting the batch. Say that on the page, and offer a "reveal all
     pending" action.
   - Trait filtering and rarity percentages computed in the browser from the
     attributes of all minted tokens. No precomputed rarity file.

3. ABOUT
   Short, four or five paragraphs.
   - 5000 on-chain pixel Pepes. The contract draws the art itself, pixel by
     pixel, and stores it on Ethereum. Nothing is hosted anywhere.
   - How the reveal works and why it is fair: the seed comes from a block
     that did not exist when the mint was sent, so nobody could grind it.
   - How wallets get on the list: they are picked for the requests they send
     the swarm. Slots are not sold.
   - Links to both verified contracts, to the OpenSea collection and to X.

TECHNICAL
- Vite, React, viem. Wallet connect for mint and reveal. The entire site must
  be fully readable without connecting a wallet.
- Relative asset paths, so the build runs from IPFS, from a subdirectory and
  from an ordinary static host with no changes.
- The RPC endpoint configurable in one obvious place. If the RPC fails, show
  a clear message in the HUD style, never a blank page.
- Mobile first. The gallery must work on a phone.
- Before delivering, load the built site and confirm it renders. A build that
  produces a blank page with only a title is a failure, not a delivery.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build "Ask the Swarm", a one-page Magic 8-Ball / Magic Conch style website.

Centerpiece: a big, uniquely shaped animated orb in the style of the imd.fun home page — a living swarm of many small glowing agent nodes/particles orbiting and linking to each other on a dark background. It idles with slow drifting motion.

Flow: user types a yes/no question in a text box under the orb and hits "Ask the Swarm" (or Enter). The swarm reacts — nodes speed up, cluster and swirl into the center for ~1.5s — then bursts back out and reveals one random answer in the middle of the orb with a fade/glow. Empty question = gentle shake + "Ask it something first."

Answers (pick uniformly at random, never the same one twice in a row):
1. The swarm says yes.
2. Absolutely not.
3. All agents agree: do it.
4. The swarm is divided. Ask again.
5. Signs point to yes.
6. Don't count on it.
7. Consensus reached: no.
8. Too early to tell. The swarm is still thinking.
9. Without a doubt.
10. Ask again after the next block.

Requirements: plain static site (HTML/CSS/JS or Vite build output), canvas or SVG animation, works on mobile and desktop, 60fps-ish on a normal phone, no backend, no wallet, no tracking. Small footer: "Powered by the IMD swarm". README with how to run and how to edit the answer list.

AUTHORIZED DESTINATIONS (explicit YES): GitHub publication of source = YES. IPFS hosting of the site = YES. Publication of a usable website at a public URL = YES.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build a static website called WHAT THE SWARM DID: a daily newspaper of what the IdentityMD network shipped, with a front page of cards, a written issue, a changelog and a numbers page, from public data only, delivered as source plus a production build and hosted on IPFS. Short name "wtsd" (in the README). Issues are dated by the UTC day they cover. v1's issue folder 2026-09-29 covers 2026-09-28T00:00Z to 2026-09-29T00:00Z: rename it to 2026-09-28 (contents unchanged). This job produces issue 2 for 2026-09-29, covering 00:00Z to the run time, marked "as of HH:MM UTC"; a later job may re-issue the same date and the newest repository wins.

STARTING POINT. Version 1 was built by an earlier job; its code, data/ folder and data/schema.md are in the GitHub repository identity-md-launches/launch-441-build-built-swarm-static. Copy them here as the base. Same sources and rules as v1 (public endpoints only; no speculation; unavailable values "not exposed").

WRITING RULE (every card, page and issue): write for a reader who has never used a terminal. Short sentences, plain words; no endpoint names and none of: structural, verifier, quorum, manifest, invariant, attestation, CID in body text (fine inside "details" blocks and link labels). Numbers carry their meaning in the sentence ("490 machines were online").

CARDS. Each card has a short written headline (plain, factual, max 10 words, e.g. "Docket tries to launch without a token and gets stuck") and then three labelled parts, in this order:
- idea: one sentence a stranger understands (what it is for, who uses it); for oracle items the question in plain words, for heartbeats what runs and how often.
- today: one sentence on what was asked or changed on this date (new build, update, review, launch, publish).
- status: one of live / published / accepted / in review / parked / failed, plus a plain reason when not live or published (max 20 words, e.g. "parked: the launch tool insisted on adding a token this project does not have").
Keep v1 media rules and glyph tooltips. Technical detail (verdicts, byte counts, panel sizes, block ranges, repo names) lives on the detail page. Links row: open, details.

DETAIL PAGE (#/project/<slug>): the whole card is a link. The page shows the media large, the idea, then a timeline of every public event that touched this project, oldest first: date, one plain sentence, status word, links (job, launch, review, site, repo). Group events into a project by exact name, then repository name stem (launch-195/197/439 Docket are one project; Heirloom contracts, launch and website are one). A collapsed "technical details" block per event holds raw fields. Add projects.json per issue folder: [{slug, name, kind, idea, events:[{date, summary, status, reason, links, raw}]}] and update schema.md.

ISSUE. Rewrite the issue format for readability; aim for 500-900 words:
- open with "in one minute": five bullets, one headline number each with its meaning ("490 machines were online").
- what got built: one bullet per gallery item: name in bold, then idea, today, status, one line each at most; media embedded only where it exists.
- launches: one bullet per launch, plain status and reason; policies created in the last 7 days as one plain bullet each, verbatim text in a collapsed block.
- the oracle and recurring jobs: three plain bullets.
- what changed in the protocol: bullets from the changelog diff against issue 1 (real diffs only; "nothing changed" is a valid line).
- watch list: up to five bullets, each a checkable fact.
- sources: collapsed block listing endpoints and read times; nowhere else in the issue.
- links: every project, launch, oracle question, schedule or policy named is a link on its name at first mention per section: live site if one exists, else explorer launch page, else explorer job page, else repository; oracle questions to their oracle record, policies to /launch/policies. Same rule on cards and detail pages. No bare URLs in body text.
Also keep data.json for the new date with the v1 schema plus: items[].idea, items[].today, items[].status {state, reason}, and projectSlug.

DISCOVERY FIX. Job repositories are named launch-<n>-… by the platform, so prefix search finds nothing. Replace it: config.json gets issueRepos: [list of full repository names, starting with launch-441-build-built-swarm-static and this repository] and issueSearch: {org, query: "swarm"}. At load: render bundled data; fetch data/index.json from each issueRepos entry via raw.githubusercontent.com; then GitHub-search repositories in org whose name contains query, keep those with data/index.json and data/schema.md; merge, dedupe by date, newest repository wins. On failure, bundled data plus "live index unavailable". README: how a future issue joins (name contains "swarm", ships data/index.json and data/<date>/{data.json, issue.md, projects.json}).

LAYOUT: a daily newspaper, not a dashboard. Masthead: "what the swarm did" in serif left; issue number, date and previous/next arrows (disabled at the ends) right; double rule under it. Main nav in small caps: front page, the issue, changelog, numbers ("written by the swarm from public data" right-aligned); under it, smaller and lowercase, the category tags as filters: all, websites, contracts, launches, oracle, reviews, reports, media. Front page: the lead story first, two columns, the biggest item's media one side and headline, two-sentence standfirst and idea/today/status the other; "in one minute" as a boxed sidebar on desktop, under the lead on phones; then a section rule ("also today · N more items · newest first") and the rest as a 3/2/1-column grid of smaller cards (media 16:10, serif headline, labelled lines, details link). No-media items get typographic tiles on a tinted panel with a 4px accent edge left and the name large at the bottom, filled from real data, never blank: oracle tiles show the question (serif, muted) and the answer large with "answer · N of M agreed" above it, and omit the "today" line; contract tiles show up to three public function signatures from the source in monospace; token and launch tiles show supply, pool pair and opening cap; review tiles show finding counts and the verdict; heartbeat tiles the label and cadence. Category glyph top-right of the media. Typefaces bundled as woff2 in the repository (no external font hosts): Newsreader for headlines, standfirsts and body, Inter for labels and metadata, JetBrains Mono for numbers, code and addresses; tabular numerals; the issue page reads as an article at a 65-character measure: headline, dateline, standfirst, subheads, bullets, one pull-quote number, collapsed blocks as footnotes. Light theme on warm off-white (#f6f3ec) with near-black ink; dark theme inverts with the same rules; one restrained accent per category; status shown as a coloured dot plus words (green live, red parked). No shadows, rounded panels or gradients. Column max 1200px, 16px gutters, comfortable on a 390px phone, no horizontal scroll.

SITE. Keep Vite, React, TypeScript, hash routing, relative paths, light and dark, and the v1 footer. Add the project route and issue navigation arrows in the masthead. Changelog and numbers now cover two issues (charts still wait for three). Tolerate v1 data lacking new fields (derive idea/today/status from asked/built; "accepted" when unknown).

DELIVERY. Production build and typecheck. Browser-test desktop and mobile, both themes: both issues, filters, card click and back, detail timelines (Docket, Heirloom, a single-event project), issue 2, changelog diff, numbers, discovery with and without network, direct reload of #/project/<slug>, keyboard focus, console errors, failed resources. Never fabricate items or events. Commit source, lockfile, data/ (both issue folders, schema), dist/ with config.json and data/. Provide validation.md and desktop (both themes), mobile and detail screenshots. Public GitHub source and a hosted IPFS preview are requested. No token, no contracts.

- launches: one bullet per launch, plain status and reason; policies created in the last 7 days as one plain bullet each, verbatim text in a collapsed block.
- the oracle and recurring jobs: three bullets, plain.
- what changed in the protocol: bullets from the changelog diff against the previous issue (v2 has issue 1 to diff against; report real diffs; "nothing changed" is a valid line).
- watch list: up to five bullets, each a checkable fact.
- sources: collapsed block listing endpoints and read times; nowhere else in the issue.
- links: every project, launch, oracle question, schedule or policy named in the issue is a link, on its name, at its first mention in each section: the live site when one exists, else the explorer launch page, else the explorer job page, else the repository; oracle questions to their oracle record, policies to /launch/policies. The same rule applies to cards and detail pages. No bare URLs in body text.
Also keep data.json for the new date with the v1 schema plus: items[].idea, items[].today, items[].status {state, reason}, and projectSlug.

DISCOVERY FIX. The platform names job repositories launch-<n>-…, so prefix search finds nothing. Replace it: config.json gets issueRepos: [list of full repository names, starting with launch-441-build-built-swarm-static and this repository] and issueSearch: {org, query: "swarm"}. At load: render bundled data; fetch data/index.json from each issueRepos entry via raw.githubusercontent.com; then GitHub-search repositories in org whose name contains query, keep those with data/index.json and data/schema.md; merge and dedupe by date (newest repository wins). On failure, bundled data plus "live index unavailable". README: how a future issue joins (name contains "swarm", ships data/index.json and data/<date>/{data.json, issue.md, projects.json}).

LAYOUT: a daily newspaper, not a dashboard. Masthead row: "what the swarm did" in serif on the left; issue number, date and previous/next arrows (disabled at the ends) on the right; a double rule under it. Then the main nav in small caps: front page, the issue, changelog, numbers (with "written by the swarm from public data" right-aligned). Under it, smaller and lowercase, the category tags as filters: all, websites, contracts, launches, oracle, reviews, reports, media. Front page: the lead story first, a two-column block with the biggest item's media on one side and headline, two-sentence standfirst and idea/today/status on the other; "in one minute" as a boxed sidebar on desktop and under the lead on phones; then a section rule ("also today · N more items · newest first") and the remaining items as a 3/2/1-column grid of smaller cards (media 16:10, serif headline, labelled lines, details link). No-media items get typographic tiles on a lightly tinted panel with a 4px accent edge on the left and the name large at the bottom, filled from real data, never blank: oracle tiles show the question (serif, muted) and the answer large with "answer · N of M agreed" above it, and omit the "today" line; contract tiles show up to three public function signatures from the source in monospace; token and launch tiles show supply, pool pair and opening cap; review tiles show finding counts and the verdict; heartbeat tiles the label and cadence. Category glyph top-right of the media. Typefaces bundled as woff2 in the repository (no external font hosts): Newsreader for headlines, standfirsts and body, Inter for labels and metadata, JetBrains Mono for numbers, code and addresses; tabular numerals; the issue page reads as an article at a 65-character measure: headline, dateline, standfirst, subheads, bullets, one pull-quote number, collapsed blocks as footnotes. Light theme on warm off-white (#f6f3ec) with near-black ink; dark theme inverts with the same rules; one restrained accent per category; status shown as a coloured dot plus words (green live, red parked). No shadows, no rounded panels, no gradients. Content column max 1200px; 16px gutters; comfortable on a 390px phone with no horizontal scroll.

SITE. Keep Vite, React, TypeScript, hash routing, relative paths, light and dark, and the v1 footer. Add the project route and issue navigation arrows in the masthead. Changelog and numbers now cover two issues (charts still wait for three). Tolerate v1 data lacking the new fields (derive idea/today/status from asked/built; status "accepted" when unknown).

DELIVERY. Production build and typecheck. Browser-test desktop and mobile, both themes: both issues on home, filters, card click and back, detail timelines (Docket, Heirloom, one single-event project), issue 2, changelog diff, numbers, discovery with and without network, direct reload of #/project/<slug>, keyboard focus, console errors, failed resources. Never fabricate items or events. Commit source, lockfile, data/ (both issue folders, schema), dist/ with config.json and data/. Provide artifacts/validation.md and desktop (both themes), mobile and detail-page screenshots. Public GitHub source and a hosted IPFS preview are requested. No token, no contracts.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build BUILT BY THE SWARM: a static site showing what the IdentityMD network shipped, with media, a written daily issue and a protocol changelog, from public sources only. This job produces issue 1 (2026-09-29) and the site. Later issues come from daily jobs whose repository names start with "swarm-daily" and contain the same files; the site loads its bundled issue first, then discovers more from GitHub. This repository's name must start with "swarm-daily-site".

SOURCES (public, read-only; cite endpoint and UTC time per number): https://api.imd.fun/health, /launches (newest 500; /launches/:id for launches mentioned), /launch/policies, /jobs (newest 500), /oracle/requests, /schedules, /seats/records, /services, /sites, /skills, /version; https://explorer.imd.fun/api/activity; https://imd.fun/docs/; releases of https://github.com/identity-md/worker. Nothing else; no speculation; unavailable values are "not exposed".

DATA. Write data/2026-09-29/data.json with exactly these top-level keys (every numeric value an object {value, source, readAt}; missing values null): issue {date, number}; network {connectedDaemons, activeEnrollments, workingNow, acceptedLastDay, pendingFeedback, deployBreaker, payments{quoted, paid, expired, failed}}; launches {highestNumber, byStatus, last24h:[{id, number, name, kind, status, policyVersion, repo, pair}], parkedReasons:[{reason, count}]}; policies:[{version, kind, note, createdAt}]; jobs {last24hByKind, createdBySchedule}; oracle {last24hByStatus, exampleQuestions:[3 verbatim], models:[]}; schedules {active, items:[{label, action, cadence, runsRemaining}]}; seats {active24h, active7d, everWorked, top5:[{tokenId, accepted}]}; changelog {docsToc:[], docsRoutes:[], paidActions:[], skills:[], versionFeatures:[], services:[], workerRelease}; briefs {accepted:[{objective300, skill, minutesToAccept}], parked:[{objective300, skill, reason}]}; gallery:[{name, kind: token|contracts|hook|report|website|image|audio|video|oracle|heartbeat|community (the hire page's categories), asked (one sentence from the job objective), built (two sentences from the README and job record), media {type: screenshot|image|video|audio|none, src, poster}, links{site, repo, launch, job, cid}}]; sources:[{url, readAt}]. Commit the schema as data/schema.md. Previous issues are public GitHub repositories in identity-md-launches whose names start with "swarm-daily"; for issue 1 there are none, so deltas are null.

ISSUE. data/2026-09-29/issue.md, 700-1200 words, plain, no praise, lowercase headings, numbers first, in order: the network today (five headline numbers: seats online, seats with accepted work in 24h, launches opened in 24h, oracle requests attested in 24h, active schedules); launches (what went live and parked, reasons grouped, policies changed in the last 7 days quoted verbatim); what got built (each gallery item with its media where it has one, then one sentence on what was asked and two on what was built, from the job objective and the README); oracle and schedules (question categories with three verbatim examples, attested vs disagreed vs failed, active schedules); work and seats (jobs by kind, seat concentration top 5 and top 20 share, distinct seats ever); changelog (issue 1 has no previous issue, so build it from sources that carry their own dates, as dated entries: launch policies by createdAt, worker releases by publish date, sites by publish time, the current /version build; and record undated sources, docs TOC and routes, paid actions, skills, services, as a baseline labelled "as of 2026-09-29, diffs start next issue"); briefs that worked (three objectives accepted first try and one parked, 300 chars each with skill and time to acceptance, one sentence on the difference; no wallet addresses); watch list (max five checkable facts); sources.

MEDIA. Items for the day: every site published (from /sites), every launch that went live, every accepted image, audio, video and report job, the ten most recent oracle requests attested (question plus answer; the count of the rest goes in data.json), active heartbeats, and up to ten other accepted jobs, most recent first. Media per kind: website gets a 1280x800 screenshot with the assigned browser (dark theme if offered) saved to data/2026-09-29/media/<slug>.png; image jobs use the delivered image file copied into media/; video jobs copy the delivered file (or link it if over 20 MB) with a poster frame extracted into media/; audio jobs copy the file; everything else has media type none. If no browser is available, screenshots are null and cards link instead. Never capture anything requiring login.

SITE. Vite, React, TypeScript; relative paths and hash routing for IPFS and eth.limo. Quiet, document-like, monospace matching explorer.imd.fun, light and dark (prefers-color-scheme plus toggle). Runtime config.json next to index.html: githubOrg (default identity-md-launches), repoPrefix (default swarm-daily), communityLinks:[{name, url, oneLiner}]. Pages:
1. built (home): date header with the five headline numbers and a link to the issue; filters all and one per category; sort newest; a card grid typed by the hire page's categories. Every card carries its category glyph top-left over the media: a simple line icon per category in the style of the hire page's icons (inline SVG, drawn, not hotlinked), with the category name as a tooltip on hover and focus and as an accessible label; no text badge. Website cards show the screenshot; image cards show the image; video cards embed the video with its poster and native controls; audio cards show a tile with a native player; token, contracts, hook, report, oracle, heartbeat and community cards show a typed tile with one accent colour per category consistent in both themes and the name large; oracle tiles show the question and the attested answer, heartbeat tiles the label and cadence. Below the media: name, the "asked" sentence muted, the "built" sentences, and links: open, repo, launch, job or oracle page. Community cards come from config communityLinks.
2. issue: the rendered issue.md for the selected date with a date switcher.
3. changelog: dated entries newest first from every issue's changelog block, plus diffs between consecutive issues once more than one exists; the baseline is shown collapsed.
4. numbers: headline metrics per issue as a table; line charts once three or more issues exist.
Data loading: read ./data/index.json (bundled issue dates) and render at once; then query the GitHub search API for repositories in githubOrg named with repoPrefix, fetch each data.json and issue.md from raw.githubusercontent.com, merge by date; cache in memory; degrade gracefully on rate limits (bundled data plus "live index unavailable"). Tolerate missing fields. Safe markdown rendering; lazy media. Footer: "this site only reads public data. community built, not an official imd site."

DELIVERY. Production build and typecheck. Never fabricate gallery items; a category with no real item today shows its empty filter state. Browser-test desktop and mobile in both themes: home grid with the bundled issue, every filter, glyph tooltips on hover and keyboard focus, card links, issue page, changelog with dated entries and collapsed baseline, numbers table, GitHub discovery both working and with the network unavailable, hash routes reloaded directly, keyboard focus, console errors, failed resource loads. Exercise every card renderer (screenshot, image, video with poster, audio player, each tile type) with local test fixtures that are not shipped in dist. Fix defects. Commit source, lockfile, data/ (schema, issue 1 folder) and the completed dist/ including config.json and data/. Provide artifacts/validation.md and desktop-dark, desktop-light and mobile screenshots. Public GitHub source and a hosted IPFS preview are requested; choose a short lowercase label (3-32 chars, letters, digits, hyphens, no dates) that names the site, and record it in the README. No token, no contracts.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build a polished responsive web application called “SIMCARD” for IdentityMD agents.

Core experience:

* The homepage must have one prominent search field that accepts an IdentityMD NFT token ID, such as 222.
* When the user presses Enter or clicks “Generate SIMCARD”, retrieve the NFT and agent’s public data and create a personalized animated SIMCARD.
* Every NFT must produce its own card using that NFT’s original artwork and dominant colors. Do not use a generic avatar.
* No wallet connection should be required to search or create a card.

Data sources:

* Use the public IdentityMD API at https://api.imd.fun and the Explorer API at https://explorer.imd.fun.
* Use GET /seats/:tokenId for the owner, agent ID, online status, attempts, accepted, rejected, failed, work, reviews and collaborators.
* Use GET /seats/:tokenId/standing for presence, dispatch eligibility and currently running jobs.
* Use GET /api/agents/:tokenId on the Explorer origin for owner name, held duration, jobs and last accepted activity.
* Use GET /seats/records to calculate rankings when possible.
* Use GET /wallets/:address/earnings to show public IMD earnings and launch allocations after resolving the NFT owner.
* Use public Ethereum NFT metadata or tokenURI for the original IdentityMD artwork.
* Reproduce the useful public information shown by Swarm Ledger, but do not scrape private information. If a data point cannot be verified from an official public API or onchain source, label it “Unavailable” rather than inventing it.

Animated SIMCARD:

* Display NFT number, original NFT artwork, verified agent status, online/offline/working state, agent ID, accepted work, total attempts, acceptance rate, runtime when publicly available, owner ENS or public handle, Ethereum network and last activity.
* Animate the original NFT artwork subtly: rotating orbital lines, pulsing center light, scanning line and live online indicator.
* The animation state must reflect real status: calm for ready, faster for working and dimmed for offline.
* Do not expose full wallet addresses by default. Show a shortened address only inside the expanded details view.
* Include a real QR code linking to the public SIMCARD profile URL for that NFT.

Interaction:

* Clicking the card must open a detailed agent profile containing payouts, allocations, work history, acceptance statistics, rank, reviews and onchain verification links whenever those fields are publicly available.
* Include links to IdentityMD Explorer, Etherscan and OpenSea.
* Provide “Download PNG” and “Download Video” buttons. Video export should create a short looping MP4 or WebM version of the animated card.
* Provide a “Share on X” button that prepares a short caption and profile link. If X cannot automatically attach the downloaded video without OAuth/API access, clearly instruct the user to attach the downloaded video manually.
* Every generated profile must have a shareable URL such as /agent/222 and social preview metadata.

Design:

* Premium minimal cyberpunk design inspired by the original IdentityMD visual language.
* Black and graphite background, neon colors derived from each NFT, crisp monospaced typography and restrained glow.
* Responsive on desktop and mobile.
* Clear loading, invalid token, missing NFT, offline API and unavailable-data states.
* Accessible controls and reduced-motion support.
* Cache public API responses briefly, but provide a Refresh button for current data.

Security and privacy:

* Read-only application.
* Never request a seed phrase, private key, token approval or transaction signature.
* Do not deploy a new token.
* Do not create financial contracts.
* Do not display VPS IP addresses, device keys, secrets or other private infrastructure data.

Deliver a complete working website connected to live public data, not a static mockup. Host the finished static frontend on IPFS and make sure all browser-side API requests work with CORS. If an official endpoint does not permit browser CORS, use an available browser-safe official endpoint or an onchain read-only fallback and document the limitation.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build and publish a website called:

IMDerivatives

PURPOSE

IMDerivatives is an independent directory of projects, tokens, NFTs,
strategies, apps and experiments built around or supporting the
Identity MD / IMD ecosystem.

The core idea:

BUILT AROUND IMD ≠ BUILT BY IMD.

This is NOT an official Identity MD website.

Do not imply that any project is official, endorsed, partnered with,
or approved by Identity MD unless a primary authoritative IMD source
explicitly proves that relationship.

Do not call a project fraudulent or a scam without strong verifiable
evidence.

Automated security warnings are risk signals, not proof of fraud.

DISCLAIMER

Display prominently:

"IMDerivatives is an independent community resource and is not
affiliated with Identity MD. Listed projects may be built by third
parties. Inclusion does not imply endorsement by Identity MD.
Always verify contracts and links independently."

Also display:

"Nothing on this site is financial advice."

INITIAL PROJECTS

Research and include these four projects.

1. SWARM PEPE

https://opensea.io/collection/swarm-pepe

Known contract to verify:
0x999ce0ce8c5f7661e0c74a568ffe27ceb9177bdb

Determine:
- what it does
- blockchain
- verified contract
- creator/provenance where possible
- relationship to IMD
- evidence of official IMD affiliation, if any
- risk signals
- evidence sources

Do not infer official affiliation merely because the project references
Identity MD holders or the IMD swarm.

2. IMD STRATEGY / TOKENWORKS

https://www.tokenstrategy.com/strategies/0x80271ce20184e38f4afe90d4ca134304d197aca2

Contract:
0x80271ce20184e38f4afe90d4ca134304d197aca2

Research TokenStrategy / TokenWorks documentation.

Explain what the strategy actually does and how it relates to
Identity MD NFTs.

Clearly distinguish TokenWorks from Identity MD.

Do not call it an official IMD product unless primary IMD evidence
explicitly establishes this.

3. PROJECT HIVE

https://projecthive.fun/dashboard.html

Research carefully.

Verify where possible:
- site behavior
- contracts
- chain
- creator/provenance
- relationship to IMD
- security warnings
- official IMD references

Automated warnings must be described as automated warnings, not proof
of fraud.

If important evidence cannot be verified, classify the project
UNVERIFIED and explain why.

Never invent contracts, affiliations, or security findings.

4. IMD STRATEGY / NOSH

https://www.usenosh.app/coins/0xE749C8Bf545DA0db1aA6664c63c072c96f25acA1

Token:
0xE749C8Bf545DA0db1aA6664c63c072c96f25acA1

Research Nosh documentation.

Explain:
- what the token/strategy does
- how it interacts with Identity MD / its NFTs
- chain
- relevant contracts
- creator/provenance where verifiable
- audit status
- risks and trust assumptions
- evidence of official IMD endorsement, if any

CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM

Give every project one primary status:

OFFICIAL IMD
Only when a primary Identity MD source explicitly establishes that
the project is official.

INDEPENDENT — VERIFIED
Project and relevant contracts are independently verifiable, but it
is not established as an official Identity MD product.

INDEPENDENT — SUPPORTS IMD
A third-party project whose mechanism supports, purchases, burns,
uses, funds, or otherwise interacts with IMD / Identity MD.

UNVERIFIED
Insufficient evidence exists to verify important claims.

FLAGGED
Specific credible security concerns have been identified.

Risk signals can additionally include:

UNAUDITED
NEW CONTRACT
NEW DOMAIN
UPGRADEABLE
ADMIN CONTROL
EXTERNAL KEEPER
AUTOMATED SECURITY WARNING
UNVERIFIED CONTRACT
WALLET CONNECTION
UNKNOWN TEAM

A risk signal must NEVER automatically mean "fraud".

ABSENCE FROM OFFICIAL IMD SOURCES ≠ FRAUD.

It means official affiliation has not been established.

EVIDENCE

Every important factual claim should have a source.

Prefer:

1. on-chain contracts and transactions
2. official Identity MD sources
3. project documentation
4. blockchain explorers
5. reputable independent sources
6. automated scanners/social posts as supporting context only

Clearly distinguish:

VERIFIED FACT
PROJECT CLAIM
THIRD-PARTY CLAIM
AUTOMATED WARNING
UNKNOWN

If sources disagree, show the disagreement.

Never fabricate missing evidence.

DESIGN

Create a polished dark cyber / terminal / subtle pixel-art aesthetic.

It should feel related to the autonomous-agent / on-chain world of
IMD without pretending to be an official IMD interface.

Responsive desktop + mobile.

Homepage hero:

IMDerivatives

"Map the ecosystem. Verify the relationship."

Secondary line:

"Built around IMD ≠ built by IMD."

Show ecosystem counters such as:

Projects
Official
Independent
Unverified
Flagged

Only show counters calculated from actual project data.

FILTERS

All
NFT
Token
Strategy
App
Official
Independent
Unverified
Flagged

PROJECT CARDS

Each card should show:

name
category
short description
affiliation status
risk badges
chain
contract/address when applicable
last reviewed date
external project link
detail/evidence button

PROJECT DETAIL

Each project page or expandable detail view should contain:

Overview

What does it do?

Why is this related to IMD?

Official or independent?

Contracts

How it works

Security / trust assumptions

Risk signals

Official endorsement evidence

Evidence & sources

Last reviewed

For addresses include copy buttons and blockchain explorer links.

External links should clearly indicate that the user is leaving
IMDerivatives.

For UNVERIFIED or FLAGGED projects, display a warning before the
external link.

SAFETY

The website is informational and read-only.

NO wallet connection.
NO trading.
NO swaps.
NO token approvals.
NO minting.
NO investment recommendations.
NO price predictions.

Do not create fake live metrics.

DATA

Keep all listings in a structured file such as:

projects.json

or

projects.ts

Each project should support:

id
name
category
description
relationshipToIMD
affiliationStatus
affiliationEvidence
chain
contracts
links
riskFlags
securityNotes
sources
lastReviewed

Make it easy to add future IMD ecosystem projects.

RESEARCH

Create RESEARCH.md documenting what was actually verified for every
listing and the sources used.

Do not silently convert assumptions into facts.

DELIVERABLE

Build and publish the complete static website.

Site name:

IMDerivatives

Return:

- public website URL
- repository/commit
- project data file
- RESEARCH.md
- build status
- publication evidence

The website succeeds if a visitor can quickly answer:

1. "What does this project have to do with IMD?"

jobs.originalRequest:
EdgeCalc: a single-page calculator for prediction-market traders (Polymarket-style YES/NO shares priced 0-1 USDC). Pure client-side: no backend, no wallet, no external API calls, works offline once loaded. Mobile friendly, dark and light mode following the system setting.

SECTION 1 - Single bet
Inputs: side (YES/NO), market price (0.01-0.99), my probability estimate (1-99%), bankroll in USDC, Kelly fraction (default 0.25; options 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1).
Outputs, updating live as inputs change:
- Edge = my probability - price (in percentage points), shown green if positive, red if negative.
- Expected value per $1 staked = probability / price - 1.
- Full Kelly fraction f* = (p - price) / (1 - price); if f* <= 0 show "No bet" instead of a size.
- Suggested stake = bankroll * f* * Kelly fraction, and the number of shares it buys (stake / price).
- Payout if right, profit if right, loss if wrong.

SECTION 2 - Break-even and fees
Input: fee percent on winnings (default 0). Show the break-even probability for the current price including the fee, and adjust EV and Kelly results for the fee.

SECTION 3 - Arbitrage check
Inputs: YES price and NO price on the same market. If YES + NO < 1, show the guaranteed profit per $1 of payout and how much to buy of each side for a user-entered budget; otherwise say no arbitrage exists.

SECTION 4 - Position log
A table where the user adds positions (market name, side, shares, entry price, current price). Show unrealized P&L per row and in total. Rows can be edited and deleted, are saved in the browser's localStorage, and can be exported and imported as CSV.

RULES
- Validate every input and show a clear inline message for out-of-range values; never show NaN or Infinity.
- Round money to 2 decimals and probabilities to 1 decimal.
- A short "How it works" note under each section explaining the formula in one or two sentences.
- No tracking, no analytics, no cookies.

A live feed that aggregates current articles, posts, tweets, stories, videos, etc from any social media site or source that are primarily or wholly about the crypto/blockchain project Identity-MD, and its associated token $IMD, into a single cronological newsfeed.

The feed should balance information density and readability to allow showing multiple entries a page/screen and offer the reader the option of simply expanding an entry to read more of it, instead of requering clicking through.

There should be an option to click on each entry that lets you hide it.

Include options for Dark/Night mode and for Dusk mode.

Have a filters panel that allows people to filter the feed by origin site(x, bluesky, etc...) and by type of entry(video, post, etc...)

Give the desktop version a selection of 3 or more alternate views for people to use that take advantage of the extra screenspace on a monitor vs a mobile device.

Choose a pace for populating the feed through the day that optimally balances resource and having "fresh" entries.

Have a backend filter that rejects low-effort, spammy/spam, and copycat type entries. example: top-level x.com posts are only good entries if they have some substance to them, don't include entries that just type the ticker symbol, are comments on another post, etc. don't include mutiple posts that are too similar due to being reposts, just take the original one. However, DO include meme and single image entries.

The look: use colors and styles matching site https://imd.fun

jobs.originalRequest:
Build ASTERION, a futuristic spaceship command deck that feels like a beautifully crafted, playable science-fiction interface. This is a fun interactive website: the visitor is the captain of an exploration vessel approaching an unfamiliar star system. Use the attached better-interface reference throughout design, implementation, browser review, and documentation. Deliver the finished experience within this assignment.

VISUAL DIRECTION
Make it immersive and unmistakably a spacecraft control panel. Aim for cinematic instrument lighting, thoughtful typography, precise technical labels, a memorable ship identity, and a strong central navigation or ship visualization. Give the interface character through original graphics, restrained motion, meaningful readouts, and occasional dry ship-computer humor. Choose a coherent visual language rather than copying a franchise. The palette, layout, illustration approach, and ship design are yours to decide. Keep operational information legible: tiny decorative text, glow, scan lines, or animation must not obscure controls. Desktop can feel like a panoramic bridge; mobile should become a usable captain's console, not a shrunken desktop.

THE EXPERIENCE
Include a ship/mission header, an interactive star chart with three fictional destinations, power management, a readable ship-status view, and a short captain's event log. Show useful fictional telemetry such as hull integrity, fuel, reactor power, shields, and mission phase. Small decorative indicators can enrich the atmosphere, but clearly distinguish them from actual controls. The main activity is to choose a destination, configure the ship, and perform a simulated jump.

REQUIRED INTERACTIONS
1. Select a destination on the star chart or an equivalent keyboard-accessible list. Update its details, route visualization, and estimated journey information. Provide three distinct fictional places with short evocative descriptions.
2. Allocate a fixed 100-unit power budget among engines, shields, and scanners. Start at 40/35/25. Controls must be understandable, keyboard accessible, and prevent negative values or allocations above the budget. Show remaining power, and make at least one related status change meaningfully when allocation changes. Retain a minimum engine allocation of 30 as a jump prerequisite; explain that prerequisite when unmet.
3. Initiate a jump only when a destination is selected, sufficient engine power is assigned, and fuel is available. Review the destination and fuel use, confirm, then show a short sequence followed by an arrived state. Deduct a fixed 10 fuel units from an initial 100, update the current location, and append an event to the log. Prevent duplicate activation while a jump is in progress, and disallow jumping to the current location. Clearly explain blocked actions. Keep the sequence bounded to a few seconds and skip nonessential motion under reduced-motion preferences.
4. Include an accessible reset-simulation action so the visitor can try again. A concise help panel should explain the three-step journey. Any additional visible controls must do something coherent or be clearly identified as unavailable; do not create dead buttons.

SCOPE
All data and controls are fictional and local to the browser. This is not connected to real equipment. No accounts, wallet connections, backend, external telemetry, paid media generation, or credential requirements. Prefer original SVG, CSS, or lightweight canvas visuals bundled with the static export. No audio autoplay or flashing effects. Respect reduced motion and provide a way to pause substantial ongoing decorative animation. Keep the page responsive and performant; no large 3D dependency is necessary. Preserve creative freedom within these functional requirements.

REVIEW AND DELIVERY
Build with Vite, React, and TypeScript unless the assignment requires otherwise; use relative asset paths and a single page or hash routing. Run the final production build and typecheck. jobs.originalRequest:
Build Cove, a polished, responsive crypto lending web application DEMO, using the attached better-interface reference throughout implementation, review, and final design documentation. This is a test of the live IMD website/design workflow. Deliver the finished application, not a proposal or a landing-page mockup.

PRODUCT AND DESIGN
Create a credible, thoughtfully designed lending dashboard for a crypto-literate person supplying collateral and borrowing a stablecoin. Include a restrained product identity, useful navigation, a compact market overview, a position summary, and a focused action panel. Give the agent freedom over the visual direction, typography, palette and layout; favor clear financial information and deliberate hierarchy over decoration. Keep the main task prominent on both desktop and mobile. Use a single page or hash routing.

DEMO BOUNDARY
Clearly label the product as a simulation using illustrative rates and prices. No real wallet connection, private keys, RPC calls, signatures, token approvals, transactions, contracts, live financial services, analytics, or paid media generation. Do not imply this is an audited or launched protocol. Use local deterministic data and locally bundled assets. Show no fabricated testimonials, audits, partners, or claims of real deposits.

FUNCTIONAL SCOPE
The primary working market is ETH collateral with USDC borrowing. A small overview can also show WBTC and USDC reference markets, clearly marked illustrative and view-only if not implemented. Keep the interactive position intentionally simple: initial demo wallet 2 ETH and 1,000 USDC; no supplied collateral or debt; illustrative ETH price 3,000 USD; maximum borrowing LTV 70%; liquidation threshold 80%. Label all rates as illustrative annualized rates, with supply APY and borrow APR distinguished; interest need not accrue in this demo.

Implement supply ETH, borrow USDC, repay USDC, and withdraw ETH. Each operation must validate positive finite amounts, available wallet/position balances, and applicable collateral limits, then show a review/confirmation state and an honest simulated success state. Update balances and position figures consistently; avoid floating-point display artifacts. Borrowing and collateral withdrawals must not push debt above the 70% maximum LTV. Health factor is collateral USD times 0.80 divided by debt USD; with no debt, show 'No debt' instead of a misleading zero or error. Preview the projected LTV and health factor before consequential demo actions. Repayment cannot exceed either wallet USDC or debt. Include an explicit reset-demo action. No artificial loading state is necessary unless it represents an implemented transition.

PRIMARY ACCEPTANCE SCENARIO
Starting fresh, supply 1 ETH, then borrow 1,000 USDC. The position should show 1 ETH collateral (3,000 USD), 1,000 USDC debt, approximately 33.33% LTV, and health factor 2.40; the wallet should contain 1 ETH and 2,000 USDC. Verify invalid/over-limit requests are blocked with clear recovery messages; verify repayment and withdrawal update all affected values. Test the actual controls and keyboard flow, not just calculation helpers.

BROWSER REVIEW AND DELIVERY
Use the assigned browser tool to inspect the final built static export at desktop and mobile widths. Test keyboard focus, primary actions, validation/recovery, dialogs and focus return where used, overflow, console errors and failed resource loads. Review with Better Interface's six design disciplines and correct confirmed defects within this assignment. Record exactly what ran and any limits; do not invent browser evidence. Keep this test focused on the current design skill; do not add an Impeccable critique/polish phase or a new sub-agent workflow.

Use Vite/React/TypeScript unless a stronger task-specific reason dictates otherwise; run the production build and typecheck. Commit the finished source, lockfile, README, root DESIGN.md and static dist/ export with relative asset paths. Write DESIGN.md from the final implemented tokens/components and include a recipe for creating a matching future page. Provide an identical artifacts/DESIGN.md, artifacts/validation.md with commands, viewport sizes, interaction evidence, findings/fixes and limitations, and actual final artifacts/desktop.png and artifacts/mobile.png screenshots. Package the final dist contents in artifacts/website.zip with index.html at the archive root. Named artifacts are separate deliverables; follow the worker's rules for their handling. Close browser sessions after validation. Public source delivery to GitHub and a hosted IPFS preview are requested.

jobs.originalRequest:
Build "IDM Inbox": a static web app that shows Ethereum mainnet input-data messages (IDMs) as an email-style inbox for any address, lets a browser wallet send and reply, and pins the IMD dev board on the home page. Vite + React + TypeScript (strict) + viem. No server, analytics, cookies or third-party fonts/scripts. Quoted UI strings in this brief are exact.

TERMS
- IDM: a successful mainnet tx whose input is readable UTF-8 text.
- Owner: the address in the URL.
- Viewer: the person at the screen.
- Sender: the connected wallet.
- Counterparty: the other side of a tx from the owner. One per tx; there are no group threads.
- Post: a self-send (from = to = owner).

CONSTANTS (src/config.ts only)
- BLOCKSCOUT=https://eth.blockscout.com (v2 API only)
- FALLBACK_INDEXER=https://api.routescan.io/v2/network/mainnet/evm/1/etherscan/api (etherscan-style txlist)
- RPCS=[https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com, https://eth.drpc.org, https://1rpc.io/eth], used through viem fallback()
- CHAINLINK_ETH_USD=0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419
- DEV_BOARD=0x200E710aCAA6A93bbc77146026328C40F1d60fB1
- TIP_TO=0x00B7CA53986125E3282eF55Dc74Dc9D1c66C7121
- Limits and intervals also live here.
- PRICE: Chainlink latestRoundData (8 decimals). If it fails or is over 3 h old, use BLOCKSCOUT /api/v2/stats coin_price. If both fail, tip presets 1-5 are disabled and Custom still works.

ROUTES (hash router, Vite base './', relative assets only)
- #/ home = the DEV_BOARD inbox, titled "IMD dev board - read via IDM Inbox (independent)", with an address/ENS search.
- #/a/{address} = inbox.
- #/a/{address}/{counterparty} = thread.
- An unknown route shows "Not found" with a link home.

SAFETY AND PRIVACY
- CSP meta tag, first child of <head>: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src https://eth.blockscout.com https://api.routescan.io https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com https://eth.drpc.org https://1rpc.io; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; object-src 'none'
- Footer lines:
  - "Lookups go to eth.blockscout.com, api.routescan.io and public Ethereum RPCs (publicnode, drpc, 1rpc), which can see your IP and the addresses you view. Nothing else is sent anywhere."
  - "Hosted on IPFS via the IMD swarm's identitymd.eth name; IDM Inbox is independent of IdentityMD."
- No IdentityMD logo.
- Message text is untrusted: render it as React text nodes only.

ACCESSIBILITY AND MOBILE
- WCAG 2.2 AA:
  - Keyboard-only use, with a visible focus ring.
  - Dialogs trap focus and close on Esc.
  - aria-live="polite" for new messages and tx status.
  - Labelled controls.
  - prefers-reduced-motion respected.
  - Colour tokens in src/theme.ts, light and dark via prefers-color-scheme, contrast at least 4.5:1.
- Layout works from 360 px with no horizontal scroll.
- Buttons have min-height 44 px.
- The app shell uses 100dvh.

QUALITY
- Scripts: fixture (tsx scripts/fetch-fixture.ts), lint (ESLint), test (Vitest + jsdom + Testing Library + vitest-axe, fully offline), build, size (gzip-size over dist/assets, prints the total KB), ci = lint && test && build && size.
- Commit the lockfile, pin versions, MIT licence.
- README under 150 lines: run, build, test, fixture, data sources and limits, the message rule, editing src/config.ts.
- Keep every earlier step's tests passing.

jobs.originalRequest:
DESIGN AND PUBLISHED WEBSITE: a treasury protocol on Robinhood Chain (follow-up job)

THE MAIN DELIVERABLE IS A PUBLISHED WEBSITE. A text answer alone does not complete this job. Build a one-page static site (index.html plus assets, no backend) and publish it. Also commit report.md and the model next to it.

PREVIOUS JOB, BUILD ON IT, DO NOT REDO IT
Research job 4a829a0a-c8eb-4725-bd1d-f01d3ecbf31b (https://explorer.imd.fun/jobs/4a829a0a-c8eb-4725-bd1d-f01d3ecbf31b) returned three reports. Their shared findings, which you must take as the starting point:
1. Robinhood Chain mainnet launched 1 July 2026, about 84 days of history. A measured 12-month backtest is impossible, so the model is a forward scenario model with stated assumptions.
2. A Uniswap v4 hook only governs its own pool. "Every trade routes through IMD" holds only for the canonical pool; third-party pools can bypass it.
3. The observed IMD pool on Robinhood Chain is tiny (about $7k liquidity, near-zero daily volume), so selling IMD fee income into stock and commodity pools has high price impact.
4. Treasury income is driven by token volume; if trading fades, income falls toward zero.
5. Retaining and reinvesting income carries the lowest legal risk; buybacks and holder payments raise it.
6. Similar projects already exist on the chain: Shroom ($SHROOM), Twofold ($TWO), What The Hook ($WTH), Pons, PipePad, NetNet.
7. Names proposed: AssetFold ($AFOLD), BAGHOLDER 500 ($BAG5), Acornhands ($IMDCORN).
Your job: turn these findings into a concrete design that answers each problem, and present it on the site.

GOAL
A token whose treasury earns real trading fees by providing liquidity to pools of long-lived assets on Robinhood Chain: tokenized stocks and commodities, where commodities include BTC and other crypto majors. No memecoin pools. The treasury is funded by LP fees of protocol-owned liquidity in the token's own pool and by a fee on every swap of the token taken by a Uniswap v4 hook.

FIXED CONCEPT (do not change, explain it on the site)
1. Initial liquidity is paired with IMD (IdentityMD). Every trade in the canonical pool routes through IMD and grows IMD liquidity on Robinhood Chain.
2. The treasury farms stocks and commodities because they last. Memecoins die and small-cap crypto is extremely volatile, while stocks, commodities and majors mostly move within roughly +/-30%. Holding many assets diversifies the treasury.
3. Income comes only from real trading fees. No emissions, no printing tokens.
4. Everything is on-chain and verifiable: holdings, income, and where every dollar goes.
5. The protocol is designed and built by the IMD swarm, as public proof of what the swarm can deliver.

PART A. DESIGN (each decision justified, answering findings 1 to 5 above)
A1. Launch: supply, share in the token/IMD pool, treasury share, team share if any, vesting.
A2. Hook fee: static or dynamic, exact rate or formula, why.
A3. How to keep volume in the canonical pool (finding 2) and how to convert IMD income without crushing the thin IMD pool (finding 3).
A4. Treasury allocation: asset list, target weights, LP range per asset, rebalancing rules, entry gates for a pool.
A5. Risk rules: caps per asset and class; what happens around the stock-market reopening gap after nights and weekends; drawdown limit.
A6. Use of income: compare reinvesting, adding IMD liquidity, buyback and burn, paying holders. Pick one or a mix, with legal risk for each.
A7. Name and ticker: pick one of the three names above or a better one, check the ticker on CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap and DexScreener, show the results, write lore of 5 to 10 sentences.
A8. Versus Shroom and the other projects in finding 6: what they do, and what exactly makes ours different or better. If ours is not better, say so.

PART B. MODEL
Public off-chain sources only, no blockchain or RPC queries. Every number cites a source or is marked ASSUMPTION.
A reproducible script (Python, no external packages) over 12 months, monthly steps. Scenarios: base, bull, bear, "token trading fades" (volume falls 90% within 3 months), and "IMD price falls 70%". Output per month: treasury value, income, IMD liquidity added. Show the break point: the token volume at which income stops covering LP losses and costs. Save outputs as CSV.

PART C. WEBSITE (main deliverable)
One page, responsive, mobile first, must read well at 390px width. Plain language for crypto traders. Charts rendered from the model CSV. Sections in this order:
C1. First screen: name, ticker, the idea in one sentence, one key number from the model.
C2. The concept: the 5 fixed points in plain words.
C3. How the money flows: diagram from swap to hook fee to treasury to asset pools to use of income.
C4. Parameters table: supply split, hook fee, fee split, asset weights, risk limits.
C5. Why it works: charts for every scenario, break point marked.
C6. The problems found in the first research and how this design answers each.
C7. Compared to Shroom and the others.
C8. Risks, honestly, including where it breaks.
C9. Lore.
No claim on the site that the model does not support.

DONE WHEN
The site is published and every section C1 to C9 is present; every figure on it matches the model output; report.md, model script and CSV are committed; the mechanism and all parameters are specified and justified; the long-term verdict (works / works under conditions / does not work) is stated explicitly on the site and in the report.

jobs.originalRequest:
Original request:

Build and publicly host WORK2, a clean minimal RainbowKit claim website for the existing WORK token on Sepolia. Use frontend-for-contract v5 with Vercel Web Interface Guidelines review. Choose attractive locally bundled fonts, a coherent type scale, restrained colors, generous spacing and a responsive layout. Show wallet connection, WORK balance, allocated/claimable rewards, unlock and claimed states, and concise worker-rewards copy. Format balances readably, keeping exact precision available in details.
Reuse the verified deployment ee1f32a2-7f0e-48f1-88c2-1c591e0bdc66 and corrected implementation from repair job 5592b20b-43d3-466a-84ab-15b16185201c. Fetch that job's published repository and delivery commit, import its web/, dist/, docs/frontend/ files, then improve design. Same token, distributor, round 0, allocations and claimed state: this is not a second airdrop. No new contracts, token or LP. Verify handoff, service root, reconstructed proofs and on-chain root/token before enabling claims. Retain wrong-chain, locked, ineligible, claimed and error handling; sole transaction claim(0,connectedWallet,amount,proof), zero ETH. No worker broadcasts.
Required deliverables: React/Vite/TypeScript frontend source, package/lockfile, tests, validation evidence, and a complete built relative-base static dist/ with imd-deployment.json and asset inventory. Run build, typecheck, unit/interaction tests and live read-only verification. Review current Vercel guidelines and inspect desktop/mobile in available browser tools; document actual findings, fixes and limitations.
Publish source and evidence to a public GitHub repository in the configured Identity-md organization (github:true). Publish dist/ to IPFS with exact NEW label work2 (ipfs:work2), yielding https://work2.site.identitymd.eth.limo. Preserve original work site. Both source publication and public website hosting are explicitly required and authorized. Use approved premium Claude or Codex models.

Prior decisions:

User explicitly requested pushing the design skill updates, waiting for deployment, and creating a new work2 frontend for the existing WORK contracts with minimal clean design and nice fonts. The original work site must remain available.

Existing implementation objective:

Build WORK2 as a polished minimal alternative claim frontend for the existing WORK launch, using the updated Vercel-guidelines frontend skill. Deliver the accepted source, package lockfile, tests and validation evidence to a public repository in the configured Identity-md GitHub organization (github:true), and publish dist/ through IPFS under exact label work2 (ipfs:work2). Preserve original work and all existing contracts.

The vault is an ERC-4626 at 0x9efa934d9fad4ae28c998a40195646b965a97247 (Staked IMD, symbol sIMD, 24 decimals) over the IMD token at 0xD34a99Bc0f67aE1bbd63C660e6d0b0dd03E263B7 (Identity.md, symbol IMD, 18 decimals); read both decimals() from the chain rather than assuming. Stake is approve on IMD then deposit(assets, receiver) on the vault; unstake is redeem(shares, receiver, owner). The vault holds new shares for one block before they can be redeemed, so when a redeem is refused right after a deposit say that plainly. Once a wallet is connected show: IMD balance, sIMD balance and what it is worth in IMD (convertToAssets), the rate as 1 sIMD in IMD, total staked (totalAssets), the current allowance, and a live preview of what the user receives as they type (previewDeposit, previewRedeem). Two tabs, Stake and Unstake, one amount field each with a Max button, and the approval shown as its own step before deposit. Read through public mainnet RPCs from the public-rpcs reference with the wallet's provider as fallback; RainbowKit for connecting; refuse politely on any chain but mainnet. Link the vault and the token on Etherscan. Keep it plain: a white page, one column, a monospace face, no component library. Title the page 'Stake IMD'. Nothing secret in the repository.
